newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close mixed in quiet session.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close mixed in quiet session.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed mixed in thin trading Monday ahead of congressional testimony Tuesday by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, dealers said.
"There was very little action today. Most players are waiting for Greenspan to speak, so the overall trading environment was guarded," one dealer said.
He said Greenspan was not expected to hint at an interest rate hike in August in his semi-annual address.
"But the U.S. economy is performing so well that the slightest word of caution by the Fed chief could spoil the bullish mood in the markets," said the dealer.
The FRB Brady bond due 2005 edged up 1/8 to 93-7/8 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 closed off $0.17 at 118.05.

"The market is regrouping, with a calmer front in Brazil and the focus shifting back to New York," another dealer said, referring to last week's devaluation fears in Brazil which hit local stock and bond prices.
